prerequisites: Good knowledge of Electromagnetism (seen in 'Física' and 'Campos y ondas' courses) and, above all, Mathematics (mainly vector calculus and operation with complex numbers; resolution of systems of linear equations and quadratic equations; trigonometry; differential and integral calculus; knowledge and use of exponential and logarithmic functions).

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Students have the capacity to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.

teaching_methods: Autonomous study of each topic, using basic and complementary bibliography.
Study of theoretical content presented and developed in the chapter.
Resolution of proposed examples throughout the chapter.
Resolution of exercises proposed at the end of the chapter, with tutor discussion.
Review of theoretical concepts for each didactic unit.
Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC), consisting of voluntary questions and simple exercises.
assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained from the Face-to-Face Exam (Prueba Presencial) and, if completed on time, Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC). The Face-to-Face Exam consists of four problems/exercises, each graded 0-10, with a minimum of 2 points required for each problem to pass the exam. If the exam score is above 4.0 and PECs were completed, the final grade is (0.15 * Continuous Assessment Grade) + (0.85 * Face-to-Face Exam Grade). If PECs are not done or not on time, the final grade is solely the Face-to-Face Exam Grade. To pass the course, the final grade must be 5.00 or higher. A maximum grade of 10 (Matrícula de Honor) cannot be obtained without completing the PECs.
